result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [ADaMDatasetTemplate]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The structural template for an ADaM dataset. twitter-card: title: >- [ADaMDatasetTemplate]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The structural template for an ADaM dataset. title: >- [ADaMDatasetTemplate]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The structural template for an ADaM dataset. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The structural template for an ADaM dataset. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_adam_templates.py#L93-L266){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature ADaMDatasetTemplate( name, label, description, dataset_class, variables=list(), natural_keys=list(), ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} An `ADaMDatasetTemplate` describes the structure of one type of CDISC Analysis Data Model (ADaM) dataset: its label and class, the variables that form its natural key, and the specifications of its variables (as [`ADaMVariableSpec`](`pointblank.ADaMVariableSpec`) objects, in order). Templates are obtained with [`get_adam_dataset()`](`pointblank.get_adam_dataset`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The template name: `"ADSL"`, `"BDS"`, `"ADAE"` or `"ADTTE"`. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The dataset label, such as `"Subject Level Analysis Dataset"`. [description]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A short description of what the dataset holds and what a record is. [dataset_class]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The ADaM dataset class, which [`validate_adam()`](`pointblank.validate_adam`) uses to choose the checks for the type of dataset. In the templates, it's the same as `name`. [variables]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[ADaMVariableSpec]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [list()]{.doc-parameter-default} : The specifications of the dataset's variables, in order. The default is an empty list. [natural_keys]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [list()]{.doc-parameter-default} : The names of the variables that together identify a record. The default is an empty list. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's look at the template for the Basic Data Structure (BDS), the structure of analysis datasets such as ADVS (vital signs) and ADLB (laboratory results): ::: {#58d51046 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb bds = pb.get_adam_dataset("BDS") print(bds.label, "|", bds.dataset_class) print(bds.description) print(bds.natural_keys) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Basic Data Structure | BDS One or more records per subject per analysis parameter per analysis timepoint. Used for efficacy, lab, vital signs, etc. ['STUDYID', 'USUBJID', 'PARAMCD', 'AVISIT', 'ADT'] ``` ::: ::: A BDS dataset has a record for each analysis parameter (`PARAMCD`) at each visit and date, for each subject. The template's properties list the required and conditionally required variables: ::: {#a4779238 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(bds.required_variables) print(bds.conditional_variables) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ['STUDYID', 'USUBJID', 'PARAMCD', 'PARAM', 'AVAL'] ['TRT01P', 'AVALC', 'BASE', 'CHG', 'AVISIT', 'ADT', 'ABLFL'] ``` ::: ::: Every BDS dataset needs the identifiers, the parameter and the analysis value. The conditional variables, such as the baseline value `BASE` and the change from baseline `CHG`, are needed only for some analyses. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_adam_dataset`) : Get the template for a type of dataset. [](`~ADaMVariableSpec`) : The specification of a variable in the template. [](`~SDTMDomainTemplate`) : The equivalent for SDTM domains. ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [required_variables](#required_variables){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | The names of the required variables, in order. | | [conditional_variables](#conditional_variables){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | The names of the conditionally required variables, in order. | | [population_flags](#population_flags){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | The names of the population flag variables, in order. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [required_variables]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The names of the required variables, in order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [required_variables]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Required variables (core designation `"Req"`) must be in every dataset of this type. [`validate_adam()`](`pointblank.validate_adam`) adds a null check for each one, and [`validate_adam_structure()`](`pointblank.validate_adam_structure`) reports the ones that are missing. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#09468939 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb pb.get_adam_dataset("ADTTE").required_variables ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['STUDYID', 'USUBJID', 'PARAMCD', 'PARAM', 'AVAL', 'STARTDT', 'ADT', 'CNSR'] ``` ::: ::: A time-to-event dataset (ADTTE) needs the parameter, the time to the event (`AVAL`), the start and event dates, and the censoring indicator (`CNSR`). This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ### [conditional_variables]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The names of the conditionally required variables, in order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [conditional_variables]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} A conditionally required variable (core designation `"Cond"`) is needed only in some situations, which the variable's `condition` describes. [`validate_adam_structure()`](`pointblank.validate_adam_structure`) reports the ones that are missing when `strict=True`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#78a90d3c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb adsl = pb.get_adam_dataset("ADSL") for name in adsl.conditional_variables[:4]: print(name, "->", adsl.get_variable(name).condition) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` TRT01A -> Required if actual differs from planned TRT01PN -> Required if treatment mapped to numeric TRTSDT -> Required if treatment start used in derivations TRTEDT -> Required if treatment end used in derivations ``` ::: ::: These are the first four conditional variables of ADSL, with the condition for each one. This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ### [population_flags]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The names of the population flag variables, in order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [population_flags]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Population flags, such as `SAFFL` (safety) and `ITTFL` (intent-to-treat), say whether each subject is in an analysis population, with the values `"Y"` and `"N"`. Only the ADSL template has them. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#50f92410 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb pb.get_adam_dataset("ADSL").population_flags ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['SAFFL', 'ITTFL', 'EFFFL', 'RANDFL', 'ENRLFL', 'PPROTFL', 'COMPLFL'] ``` ::: ::: [`validate_adam()`](`pointblank.validate_adam`) checks each of these flags that is a column of the data. This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [get_variable()](#get_variable){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Get the specification of a variable. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [get_variable()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Get the specification of a variable. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_adam_templates.py#L230-L266){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature get_variable(name) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The variable name. This is case-sensitive, and ADaM variable names are in upper case. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ADaMVariableSpec | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The specification of the variable, or `None` if the template has no variable with that name. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#cd8a8e34 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb adtte = pb.get_adam_dataset("ADTTE") adtte.get_variable("CNSR") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` ADaMVariableSpec(name='CNSR', label='Censor', dtype='Num', core='Req', required=True, max_length=None, controlled_term=None, source=None, condition=None, is_population_flag=False) ``` ::: ::: `CNSR` is the required censoring indicator of a time-to-event dataset. A name that isn't in the template gives `None`: ::: {#431535bb .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(adtte.get_variable("AESEQ")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` None ``` ::: ::: `AESEQ` belongs to the ADAE template, not to ADTTE.
